_: The python-docx members docx4j_py.docx promises, derived from an installed python-docx 1.2.0 by scripts/python_docx_subset.py. Do not edit by hand; run the script in a throwaway venv that has python-docx.

omitted_enums.WD_BUILTIN_STYLE: 163 members naming Word's built-in styles by an MS API integer; docx4j_py.model.content.styles.BUILT_IN_STYLES is the same list keyed by style id and display name, which is what a style setter takes

Run.name: mark_comment_range
Run.reason: python-docx's internal helper for add_comment; Phase G places the three markers itself, hoisting them out of a w:ins (CR-003 section 15.2)

RenderedPageBreak.name: following_paragraph_fragment
RenderedPageBreak.reason: the other half of the same split; see preceding_paragraph_fragment

RenderedPageBreak.name: preceding_paragraph_fragment
RenderedPageBreak.reason: splits a paragraph at a rendered page break into two detached Paragraphs; nothing in this engine renders, so nothing writes the break it needs

_Cell.name: merge
_Cell.reason: python-docx's rectangular merge is about 150 lines of grid surgery whose failure mode in Word is a repair prompt; Phase J left it out rather than half-implement it (CR-003 section 20)

Styles.name: latent_styles
Styles.reason: 371 w:lsdException entries behind an API nothing in the wild uses; the typed w:latentStyles is document.styles.element.latent_styles

Comments.name: add_comment
Comments.reason: an unanchored comment, which Word shows nothing for; Phase G has no verb for one and Document.add_comment(runs, text) is the anchored form

Drawing.name: image
Drawing.reason: python-docx's Image proxy is a whole image-format parser (blob, dpi, content_type, native size); this engine reads the header it needs in docx4j_py.wml.pictures and hands the bytes out through the content API's InlinePicture.get_bytes() and .image_part
